campaign.title: Recombine the RCS coefficient and test the Hardy return map

conductor_policy.monitoring: Track every H_D floor, dyadic L and D weight, odd-q restriction, endpoint star, and stationary error. Do not replace a localized divisor sum by r_2 until the partition identity is exact.
conductor_policy.round_close: Close after exact single-block algebra, global partition bookkeeping, a Hardy/Voronoi normalization comparison, and a verdict on whether the global estimate is strictly weaker or circular.

numerical_purpose: falsify a proposed exact finite coefficient identity
resource_policy.numerical_prohibition: Finite agreement cannot prove a global radial-sum estimate.
resource_policy.literature_policy: Use primary sources for Hardy or truncated Voronoi formulas and audit exact constants, truncations, and errors.

frozen_target.coefficient_identity: For n=hq, prove the cancellation of the stationary h powers against the Vaaler 1/h and retain the exact Phi and shell factors.
frozen_target.recombination_question: Sum actual L and D partitions and determine whether the coefficient becomes r_2(n)/4 times an n-only symbol or a precisely localized angular divisor sum.
frozen_target.success: Derive a strictly weaker global sufficient estimate with controlled errors, or rigorously prove that the route is a return to an equivalent Hardy/Bessel object and isolate any noncircular remainder.

exit_gates: D/L recombination including Phi and floor heights
campaign.promotion_policy: A global recombination promotes only if all partitions and errors are exact and the resulting sufficient estimate is proved to be logically weaker than the existing blockwise target.

closing_assessment.main_result: The active M1 aggregate has an exact angular divisor coefficient and a weaker global estimate; M1 alone does not collapse to r_2/4, while full radial completion is the Hardy--Voronoi return map.
